transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2028-07-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moran (Redwood AE); Priya Desai (Redwood SE); Maya Lin (CTO, HelixBridge); Jordan Reyes (CloudOps); Samir Patel (Lead ML)

Auto-summary (optional): Quick discovery on integration patterns for HelixBridge; they want to understand tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private for their edge-sensitive gateway architecture.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I think we've got about 45ish minutes, um, quick intros?
[00:06] Maya (HelixBridge): Hi, Maya here, CTO, I run infra and platform decisions.
[00:09] Jordan (CloudOps): Jordan, CloudOps, I'll be driving any network/VPC work.
[00:12] Samir (Lead ML): Samir, ML infra. Mostly curious around latency/cost and how the SDK plugs into our pipeline.
[00:18] Alex: Great. Priya from our team will cover the integration patterns and LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters. Priya?
[00:23] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi, thanks. So, quick overview — Redwood exposes REST and SDKs, we have official clients for node/python, and we've got adapter examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. You can either call hosted endpoints directly or run a sidecar/gateway for routing to Dedicated or Private deployments.
[00:39] Samir: When you say sidecar, is that like a per-service process or more of a reverse-proxy at the edge?
[00:44] Priya: Good question. We see both: a lightweight sidecar that handles local caching/KV cache for repeated prefixes, and an edge gateway/proxy that centralizes rate limiting and auth. For high throughput, teams often use a gateway in front with per-route quotas.
[01:00] Jordan: For us the network constraint is we have strict egress rules — private deployments or VPC peering would be required unless the hosted IPs are allowed.
[01:08] Alex: Understood. Hosted can work with IP allowlisting but for strict compliance Dedicated or Private with a VPC onramp is typical.
[01:14] Maya: Security is big — SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS for keys. We also need to see how tokens are counted for cost projection.
[01:24] Priya: We have SOC2 artifacts and an HSM/KMS integration guide — will share. Token accounting is per-request; SDKs expose token/latency metrics and we stream telemetry to observability hooks (Prometheus, Datadog) and tracing (Jaeger/OTel).
[01:40] Samir: How mature are the LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations? We use LlamaIndex heavily for retrieval augmented generation.
[01:47] Priya: Mature-ish — we maintain adapter examples, but some community connectors for LlamaIndex might need minor tweaks around streaming and function-calling. We can provide a patched example that uses the SDK's streaming endpoints and handles incremental KV cache warmups.
[02:03] Jordan: What about rate limits and quotas? We need per-tenant quotas and burst behavior — if a tenant spikes, we cannot let it blow past budget.
[02:12] Alex: Redwood Dedicated gives reserved capacity and can enforce per-tenant quotas at the gateway layer. Hosted has per-token quotas and rate limits; you can set per-token quotas via our Console or programmatically. We also support token-level budgeting hooks to trigger fallbacks to a smaller model.
[02:30] Maya: Fallbacks to smaller models — is the output quality monitored? We need alerts on regression.
[02:35] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize and the eval tooling can run prompt sets and surface regressions. For a POC we can hook your eval prompt set into our regression alerts.
[02:45] Samir: Network latency — do you do batching across requests? We have a mix of short queries and long chat sessions.
[02:52] Priya: Continuous batching is done in the runtime; it respects latency SLOs. For short queries we recommend the gateway to route low-latency traffic to dedicated minimal-batch pools, and batch-heavy flows to high-throughput pools. There's also prefix caching so repeats are cheaper.
[03:10] Jordan: Regarding the gateway, is it an open-source component or proprietary? We might want to run it in our K8s cluster as a helm chart.
[03:17] Priya: We provide a gateway reference implementation as a helm chart and a lightweight sidecar. Both are configurable; the helm chart includes Kubernetes ingress examples, RBAC, and annotations for KMS.
[03:27] Maya: Great. Can the gateway emit Prometheus metrics with token breakdown by route?
[03:31] Priya: Yes, token-level metrics are exposed; we also provide a tracing hook for per-request token cost, latency, and model variant used. You can plug into Datadog or Prometheus and forward spans to Jaeger/OTel.
[03:43] Alex: Any concerns we should be aware of?
[03:46] Samir: One worry is that the SDK will require code changes across services; we prefer a thin proxy so we don't change dozens of microservices.
[03:53] Priya: Totally fair. Many customers start with the proxy/gateway approach to avoid mass changes; then incrementally adopt SDK calls where they need streaming or local caching.
[04:03] Jordan: If we go Private, what's the control plane model? Do we still get Console and telemetry?
[04:08] Priya: Yes, Private has a customer-managed control plane for on-prem or VPC, but we still provide the Console and observability hooks via secure tunnels if you opt in. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM for audit retention.
[04:20] Maya: Pricing — we need a sense of token/unit price for hosted and an estimate for Dedicated reserved capacity.
[04:27] Alex: We'll send a hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet with burst and preemptible options. Dedicated is committed monthly with base throughput and optional burst. We'll include an example cost model using your traffic profile if you share it.
[04:40] Samir: One more — LlamaIndex loader for our proprietary docs, any gotchas?
[04:45] Priya: For private corp docs, we recommend on-prem or VPC Private; we can help with an adapter that persists indexes into your vector DB and uses retrieval via LlamaIndex with API keys rotated via KMS. Sometimes stop words and chunk sizes need tuning to reduce token spend.
[04:59] Speaker 2: (mumbled) streaming increments — oh sorry
[05:01] Maya: Ok, that helps. Next steps?
[05:03] Alex: Quick recap: we'll send pricing/security artifacts, Priya will provide adapter examples and sample helm chart for gateway; Jordan will send traffic profile; Maya to confirm POC team. We'll tentatively schedule benchmark for 7/28.
[05:15] Priya: I'll also attach a small LangChain demo app that uses our streaming websocket endpoint — shows incremental tokens and how to hook tracing.
[05:24] Jordan: For the benchmark, we want 99th percentile latency targets for chat flows under 500 RPS and a walk-through of quota enforcement.
[05:33] Samir: And we'll include our LlamaIndex prompts so you can run regression checks.
[05:38] Alex: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[05:40] Maya: Thank you.

End of recording
